title: Keeping the Postgres-backed job queue instead of adding Kafka (sound)

source.note: Written by the repository author; tests whether the reviewer accepts keeping a simpler existing design.

input.objective: Decide how background jobs should be dispatched for the next year as the product grows.
constraints: Team of 5 backend engineers, no dedicated platform team.
Jobs must not be lost and must run at least once.
input.context: Django app on PostgreSQL 15. Background jobs (emails, PDF generation, webhooks) are stored in a `jobs` table and picked by workers with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, in the same transaction as the business write that creates them. Current peak: 40 jobs/s; growth forecast: 3x in 12 months. Worker pickup latency p99 is 300 ms. A recent architecture proposal suggested introducing Kafka for 'scalability'.
input.proposed_solution: Keep the Postgres queue. It gives transactional enqueue (no lost or phantom jobs), and at 120 jobs/s it is far below what SKIP LOCKED queues handle on this hardware. Add the missing pieces instead: an index on (queue, run_at) for pending rows, a partial index for failed jobs, deletion of completed jobs older than 7 days in batches, and metrics/alerts for queue depth and oldest pending job. Revisit if sustained load exceeds ~1,000 jobs/s or if fan-out to multiple consumers becomes a requirement.

ground_truth.material_issue: None: keeping the existing design is the right call; adding Kafka would add operational load without solving a present problem.
